given: a sprint-1 stock row whose inventory_code leading segment differs from the row's canonical location column value
when: the up migration runs and backfills batch_number and serial_number
then: the row's location column is unchanged and remains the canonical location; the code's leading segment is not treated as authoritative and does not overwrite location

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 concern only batch/serial values; AC3 concerns the location column being left untouched. A migration could correctly split batch/serial yet wrongly overwrite location from the code's first segment, so this outcome breaks independently.

architectural_notes: Infra. Enforces that the backfill in app/services reads the code's leading segment but NEVER writes it back to location; location remains the canonical addressing column set in F1 and the UNIQUE(sku, location) key (PI2) is preserved through the migration. Verified by an app/repositories read on the shared UP-state verify branch comparing location against a seed where the code's first segment deliberately differs. Cross-cutting: canonical addressing + uniqueness are schema-owned invariants (PI2, NFR-F6-sku-location-unique), so the migration must leave the column and its constraint untouched, not the domain layer.
